status_detail: drug_exposure is now 96.8% mapped (reference_paper_extraction.md section 9a), so drug-concept mapping is no longer the blocker. Remaining blockers: (1) ICU infusions (inputevents) are outside the OMOP ETL scope, so albumin and the crystalloid infusions that define time zero are absent -- see docs/mimic_omop_coverage_workplan.md workstream B; (2) the Sepsis-3 population must be reconstructed, not taken from a condition code -- workstream C.3; (3) baseline covariate coverage (reference uses 24 features, first_pass_covariates has 9).
source_question: Among adult ICU patients with sepsis, what is the effect of crystalloids plus albumin versus crystalloids alone, both initiated within the first 24 hours of the ICU stay, on 28-day all-cause mortality?

target_trial.population: Adults with sepsis admitted to ICU
target_trial.treatment: Crystalloids plus albumin, both given within the first 24 hours of the ICU stay, with the first albumin dose after the first crystalloid dose
target_trial.comparator: Crystalloids only within the first 24 hours of the ICU stay (no albumin in that window)
target_trial.time_zero: First crystalloid administration within the first 24 hours of the ICU stay (inclusion_start); NOT ICU admission itself
eligibility_criteria: Sepsis-3 during the ICU stay (SOFA >= 2 with suspected infection, the latter defined by an antibiotic course plus a body-fluid culture within the Sepsis-3 timing window), reconstructed from measurement / drug_exposure / culture records -- NOT from a sepsis condition-occurrence code: a diagnosis-code phenotype gives ~3,048 patients versus the reference ~18,421 (see concept_audit.md and reference_paper_extraction.md sections 2a and 9)
First ICU stay per patient only
Survived and remained in the ICU for at least 24 hours (ICU length of stay >= 1 day)
At least one crystalloid administration within the first 24 hours of the ICU stay -- this is the inclusion trigger and defines time zero; patients with no crystalloid in that window are excluded
target_trial.assignment_procedure: Not randomized; treatment arm (crystalloids plus albumin vs. crystalloids alone) is determined by the treating clinician's choice within the exposure-eligibility window, i.e. the first 24 h of the ICU stay (which contains time zero, the first crystalloid dose); an observational target-trial emulation, not an RCT.
target_trial.censoring_strategy: Administrative censoring at the earlier of end of the observed data (observation period) or 28 days after time zero, for anyone who has neither died nor been observed for the full follow-up window.
target_trial.analysis_strategy: Intention-to-treat analog: treatment status is fixed by exposure within the 24-hour exposure-eligibility window and not updated afterward; a later crossover between arms is not accounted for.
target_trial.treatment_value: Crystalloids plus albumin, both initiated within the first 24 hours of the ICU stay (albumin after the first crystalloid)
target_trial.comparator_value: Crystalloids only, no albumin within the first 24 hours of the ICU stay

design_constraints: Align eligibility, treatment assignment, and start of follow-up to prevent immortal-time bias
Use only covariates measured before or during the predefined baseline window
Do not promote text-matched concepts to executable concept sets without human validation

target_trial.grace_period_hours (24) is the exposure-eligibility / ascertainment window: both the first crystalloid dose and the first albumin dose must fall within the first 24 h of the ICU stay, and albumin must come after the first crystalloid (i.e. after time zero). It is not a grace period for outcome-free survival in the usual target-trial sense. The reference authors argue 24 h is short enough that the induced immortal time is negligible and test that claim by re-running the exposure-eligibility window at 6 h / 24 h / 72 h of the ICU stay (reference_paper_extraction.md sections 3 and 7a).

time_zero / follow-up clock: the reference study starts follow-up and all effect estimates at the first crystalloid administration within the first 24 h of the ICU stay (inclusion_start), not at ICU admission. icu_time_zero.json still anchors on ICU admission because ICU infusions (inputevents) are outside the current OMOP ETL scope (reference_paper_extraction.md section 9a); realign to first-crystalloid once infusion data is available.

secondary_estimands: the age effect modifier is dichotomised >=60 vs <60 for subgroup display, with continuous admission_age also fed to the CATE model; 'septic shock' is a derived pre-treatment clinical state (vasopressor + lactate >= 2; see concept_sets.septic_shock.note), not condition concept 196236 (reference_paper_extraction.md section 8).

eligibility_criteria/assignment_procedure/censoring_strategy/analysis_strategy/effect_measure/treatment_value/comparator_value (added 2026-08-07, corrected 2026-08-29 against reference_paper_extraction.md) are aligned to the reference paper and the authors' analysis code (soda-inria/causal_ehr_mimic); the paper itself under-specifies several of them, so the code is the authoritative source -- verify against both before treating them as an exact restatement of the published protocol.

sepsis.note: 132797 is the standard SNOMED 'Sepsis' concept and a legitimate concept-mapping benchmark target (reference_concept_mappings.json), but it must NOT define the study population: a diagnosis-code phenotype yields ~3,048 patients vs the reference ~18,421. The population needs a reconstructed Sepsis-3 phenotype (SOFA >= 2 with suspected infection) -- see eligibility_criteria and docs/mimic_omop_coverage_workplan.md workstream C.3.

septic_shock.note: 196236 is the standard SNOMED 'Septic shock' concept (a valid concept-mapping benchmark target), but this effect modifier is a derived pre-treatment clinical state, not a diagnosis code. Per the authors' code (caumim.variables.selection.get_septic_shock_from_features): Sepsis-3 positive AND on a vasopressor (dopamine / epinephrine / norepinephrine / phenylephrine / vasopressin / dobutamine / milrinone) AND serum lactate >= 2 mmol/L -- the code filters >= 2, the Sepsis-3 text says > 2. See design_constraints and reference_paper_extraction.md section 8.

care_site_names: Neuro Surgical Intensive Care Unit (Neuro SICU)

published_benchmarks.source: S5 Fig selection flowchart, doi:10.1371/journal.pdig.0000721. The main-text prose '18,121' (p.8) is a typo; the S5 Fig value 18,421 is internally consistent (20,288 - 1,867 = 18,421; 3,559 + 14,862 = 18,421) and is the correct figure.
published_benchmarks.note: Check the cohort step stepwise against these counts, not only the final eligible total. The large drop is the Sepsis-3 step (40,279 -> 20,288); a diagnosis-code sepsis phenotype will not reproduce it.
